title: SA/161/2015 of Arun Kumar Sharma Vs Smt. Rama Rani

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(1) Second Appeal No.161 of 2015
Arun Kumar Sharma
ÖÖ. Appellant/Plaintiff
Versus
Smt. Rama Rani
 ....Ö. Respondent/Defendant
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Ashish Sinha, Adv. for the appellant.
Mr. Siddharth Singh with Mr. Xitij Kaushik, Adv. i/b Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocates for the respondent.
(2) Second Appeal No.162 of 2015
Arun Kumar Sharma
ÖÖ. Appellant/Plaintiff
Versus
Smt. Rama Rani
 ....Ö. Respondent/Defendant
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Ashish Sinha, Adv. for the appellant.
Mr. Siddharth Singh with Mr. Xitij Kaushik, Adv. i/b Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocates for the respondent.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Since both the appeals have arisen out of the
same judgment rendered by learned Second Additional
District Judge, Roorkee (Haridwar) on 17.7.2015, hence are
being taken up together for admission by this Court.
 Having heard the rival submissions put forth by
learned counsel of either party, it transpires that the
dispute pertains to a shop, the admitted owner whereof is
Smt. Shyam Lata, who succeeded the same from her
husband. Twenty years back, the shop, in question, was
under tenancy of one Mr. Khushi Ram, against whom the
proceedings u/s 21 of the U.P. Urban Buildings
(Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Act, 1972, were
initiated by the Landlord and such shop could be got

2
vacated in August, 1998 to be used by its owner. But
unfortunately, husband of Smt. Shyam Lata had lost his
life by that time, so she started to run that grocery shop at
her own. Since, she was also having a daughter, deserted
by her husband, living with Smt. Shyam Lata, so the whole
circumstances found such a plot that at the initiation of
her own son Ram Gopal (close friend of one Subodh
Kumar), she agreed to handover possession of said shop to
Mr. Arun Kumar Sharma (real brother of Subodh Kumar)
and thus, Mr. Sharma succeeded Smt. Shyam Lata in the
shop to run the same.
 The only question between the parties is whether
the transfer of such shop from Smt. Shyam Lata to Mr.
Arun Kumar Sharma, was in the form of a ëLeaseí or a
ëLicenceí. It was vociferously argued by Mr. Arvind
Vashisth, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the
appellant, that such transaction was definitely a ëLeaseí
and in any case, it was not a ëLicence. This assertion is in
quite contrast of the facts as are being asserted (vice versa)
by Smt. Shyam Lata, who, over the time, was succeeded by
her daughter Smt. Rama Rani. The fact which cannot be
lost sight of is that since Mr. Ram Gopal (S/o Shyam Lata)
was a government servant somewhere, so the
circumstances were not suitable for him, to run that shop
himself.
 Learned Senior Counsel has vehemently argued
that both the courts below (in their concurrent judgments,
except on the question of quantum of Licence Fee) have
wrongly shifted the burden upon the appellant asking him
to prove himself as a ëlesseeí. Rather, the burden must
have been discharged by Smt. Shyam Lata and then by her

3
daughter Smt. Rama Rani to prove themselves as the
ëLicensorí.
 It can also significantly be noted here that the
Original Suit No.78 of 2004 was initiated on 24.5.2004 by
Mr. Arun Kumar Sharma against Smt. Shyam Lata, seeking
prohibitory injunction against his eviction, except in
accordance with the provisions of law, and probably, when
Smt. Shyam Lata became acquainted about the initiation of
this litigation, then she launched the Original Suit No.12 of
2005, seeking mandatory injunction against Mr. Sharma
for evicting him from the shop in question and delivering
possession as a consequence.
 By entering deep into the merits as also the
sequence of litigation, the Court is of the opinion that the
burden was firstly upon Mr. Arun Kumar Sharma to prove
himself as a tenant (as claimed by him) because had the
Original Suit No.12 of 2005 been not filed, then O.S. No.78
of 2004, initiated at the instance Mr. Sharma, must have
failed, in case he could not be able to prove himself as a
tenant in the premises in question. Otherwise also, Mr.
Sharma is the immediate beneficiary of the shop, in
dispute, so for this reason too, he was bound to discharge
his primary burden first, rather than to shift it on Smt.
Rama Rani, because she has been admitted as a landlady/
owner of the shop, in question.
 That apart, considering the merits of the case, to
some extent, it is abundantly clear that Mr. Arun Kumar
Sharma stepped in the shop, in October, 1999 and he
claims only a single receipt of the rent issued under the
alleged signatures of Smt. Shyam Lata at that very time
and such receipt too has been found to be forged in the

4
report submitted by the Forensic Science Laboratory.
Otherwise also, Mr. Sharma could not show even a little
single evidence to prove that he ever paid any amount
towards the rent for last 17-18 years i.e. eversince he came
into possession of such shop.
 In view of the above discussion, I find that no
substantial question of law, at all, arises in both these
matters. Thus, both the appeals, being bereft of any merit,
are dismissed at the admission stage itself.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 07.10.2015
Rdang
